gates.decides: Which mutants are made from the syntax tree of a file: the twelve mutators, their replacements, what is left alone, and the order that numbers them
gates.impact: A decision gets no mutant, so a test that does not check it is never found; or a number moves and the mutants no longer are the ones test_gates 0.1.0 made of the same file

gates.decides: Which mutants are made from resolved types: which member of which receiver is exchanged for which, where a number, a guard, a branch and a returned value are mutated, and where they are not
gates.impact: A member of a class of the project is taken for one of the SDK and mutated into something else, or a guard on null gets no mutant that compiles and its tests are never asked

gates.decides: What a mutant does to a source, and the order of the mutants of a file
gates.impact: The file that is tested is not the mutant that is reported, or two mutants at one place change numbers between runs

gates.decides: The status of a mutant from its test run, the test command and the time limit, the numbers of the mutants, the report, what a run with --only or --force keeps, and whether a result of the last run may be reused
gates.impact: A mutant the tests did not notice is reported as killed, a place in the report points at other code, or an outdated result is reused after the file, its tests or the command changed

gates.decides: Which mutants of a file a part of a run with --shard takes, what a value of --shard is, and how a report says that it is a part
gates.impact: A mutant belongs to no part and is never run, or the report of a part is taken for the report of a whole run

gates.decides: Whether the reports given to merge are all parts of one run, each exactly once, and the result each mutant gets in the report of the whole run
gates.impact: A part that is missing, given twice or made from another source goes unnoticed, and mutants that were never run pass as killed

gates.decides: The page of --html: how the report is put into a script, what is escaped, where the viewer comes from, and which file counts as such a page
gates.impact: A source that holds </script> breaks the page or runs as markup in the reader's browser, or --html overwrites a file that is not a report

gates.decides: Whether a plan file is well formed, which paths are inside the package, where the test of a file is looked for, what is a glob, and which files --only selects
gates.impact: A path outside the package is mutated, a file is tested with the wrong tests, or a misspelt --only becomes a run on nothing

gates.decides: Which command-line arguments belong to this tool, their values and defaults, and what is handed to the test command
gates.impact: A typo in an option is silently ignored, or --force and --only are dropped and a weaker run is taken for the full one

gates.decides: How many test runs are started at a time, what is left out of a working copy, and whether a package can be run from a copy at all
gates.impact: The tests of a copy read the files of the package itself, where no mutant is, and every mutant survives or none does; or the default starves the machine and mutants time out

gates.decides: Whether a lock that could not be taken is held by another run, and who that run is
gates.impact: A second run starts in a package where one is at work and takes the mutant of the first for a leftover, or a file system without locks is reported as another run

gates.decides: What counts as an object and as a list of strings when a plan, a report, a package configuration and the results of the last run are read, and when two JSON values are the same
gates.impact: A file of another shape is read as valid and the run works from wrong data instead of refusing it, or a result is reused, or a part is merged, although what it was made from differs

gates.decides: How much of the output of a failed test run is shown
gates.impact: The lines that say why the tests fail without a mutant are cut off

gates.decides: Where a mutant can be built into its file as a choice made while the program runs, what the file is with the choices in it, which mutants are left out (a constant, a part), and whether a program has the static types of another outside a node
gates.impact: The program without a mutant at work is no longer the one that was there, or the one with a mutant at work is not that mutant, and a mutant is reported as killed by tests that would not have noticed it

gates.decides: The test file that runs the tests of a file on one built-in mutant, in an isolate of its own, the plan and the command of the start of the test runner that the mutants of a file share, which test files cannot be called that way, which mutants its report shows as killed, which get a start of their own or are left to the next test run, how long a mutant may take, and from when on how much memory
gates.impact: A mutant is reported as killed although the tests no longer pass without a mutant, a mutant that never ends holds the whole run, or the failure of one mutant is counted for another

gates.decides: Which test command can run the test files of many mutants of a Flutter package in one start, the test file of a mutant and what it compares before it runs its tests, which test files cannot be called that way, what the report of the test runner says of each of them, and whether a start ended the way its report says
gates.impact: A mutant is reported as killed on a test that failed for what the tests of another mutant left, on an error of the test runner, or on a report that belongs to another test file

gates.decides: Which processes belong to a test run and how much memory they hold together, how much a test run may hold after a run without a mutant, and what the report says of a run that was ended for it
gates.impact: A test run that takes memory without end is not ended before the machine has none left, a run is ended for the memory of processes that are not its own, or a limit below what the tests need turns mutants they would not have noticed into timeouts

candidates.decides: The version that is in the report and in the key of a reused result
candidates.blocker: A constant. A test keeps it equal to pubspec.yaml

candidates.decides: Which command runs, and the exit code for wrong usage and for a file that cannot be read or written
candidates.blocker: Imports dart:io (FileSystemException) and the command, so it is not a pure module. The argument rules it uses are in args.dart, which is a gate

candidates.decides: The order of the steps of a run and of a merge, what is printed, when a file is written and put back, and the exit code
candidates.blocker: Reads and writes files, copies the package and starts processes. The decisions it acts on are taken in the gates; what is left is tested with a stand-in for the test runner in test/commands

candidates.decides: The analysis session and which errors count against a mutant, how files are found, copied and locked, and how a process and its descendants are ended
candidates.blocker: dart:io and the analyzer's session throughout. Tested against real files, a real analysis and real processes in test/ and test/commands
